analogs.covers: Body and stamina: a tireless trunk climber that races up the tallest trees again and again, leaps from crown to crown, chatters at every threat and hoards whatever it finds
Voice and temper: a brilliant mimic with a long memory for faces that swoops screeching at anything near its nest tree and lives in noisy, bickering groups

headline: A grey squirrel with a magpie's voice: the Microraptor of the big forests that climbs the tallest trunks without tiring, copies every call and dive-bombs anything near its nest tree.

setting.label: The big forests: Redwoods, Wollemi, Twisted and Cedrus Forest
setting.note: Gui hatch in Redwoods, Hollow Hills, Wollemi Forest, East Passage, Twisted Forest and Cedrus Forest. Hollow Hills (grassy hills) and East Passage (a salt channel) are the blurred edges of the range. Border land: the giant trees of Big Tree Overlook, which is also every subspecies' courtship ground, and Steep Run. Everything else is roaming ground. Lives in the canopy, never in caves.

playsLike: You are a Gui, the climbing subspecies: you hatched in one of the big forests and have more stamina when climbing trees high distances. You are the smallest carnivore on the roster (Tiny, 500 combat weight, 400 HP, a 40 bite that only hurts targets under 600 combat weight, land sprint 825 for 400 s). You climb trunks and cliffs, glide from tree to tree and sleep in short bursts high up, never in caves. You live on carrion, insects and critters and hunt only Juvenile-and-younger Deinonychus, Latenivenatrix, Psittacosaurus and Struthiomimus, even guarded ones, plus Rhamphorhynchus, with at most one partner. Your weapon is mimicry: copied calls lure the parents away from their nest. In a scurry of up to 10 you swarm and dive-bomb anything that hunts you, except Apex carnivores and the six species you always flee from; as a pair or alone you may claim an Apex carnivore as your companion, ride on its side and learn its calls.

why.text: Gui “exhibit more stamina when climbing trees high distances”. Grey squirrels run up and down tall trunks many times a day and come down head first as easily as they go up (official inspiration: gray squirrels).
Gui are born mostly in the big forests of the island, Redwoods, Wollemi, Twisted and Cedrus Forest, the old, tall woods where grey squirrels thrive.

Nests “are heavily decorated with items of interest”, and in a scurry a new object is “relocated frequently”. Grey squirrels hide food in hundreds of caches and move them again when they feel watched.
“At the first sign of aggression towards them, they flee, typically accompanied with fearful cries.” A grey squirrel bolts up the trunk with a loud alarm chatter and a flicking tail.

Microraptor “are most commonly known for their mimicry of other species” and parrot calls back at tolerant species in “conversations”. Australian magpies are among the best vocal mimics, copying other birds, dogs and even sirens.

Any intruder on a claimed nest tree is “met immediately with loud, screeching protests, with members swooping overhead repeatedly”: the magpie's swooping season, with small pecks included (official inspiration: magpies).

notLike: Grey squirrels leap from crown to crown but cannot glide; Microraptor glides from trunk to trunk.
Grey squirrels live on nuts and seeds; Microraptor lives on carrion, insects and critters.
Hollow Hills and East Passage are Gui hatching areas in the profile, although they are grassy hills and a salt channel, not forest.
twist: The forest subspecies: where the others glide away, a Gui simply climbs higher and stays up longer.
